metadata.title: Kunskaper, värderingar och engagemang i medborgar-, demokrati- och samhällsfrågor hos svenska 14-åringar i ett internationellt perspektiv

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a national report for ICCS 2016 describing results for Swedish students in grade 8 (age 14). It reports descriptive and comparative statistics (e.g., mean scale scores, percentiles, and statistically significant differences) but does not provide methodological details about the complex survey design or the use of sampling/replicate weights. The report states that ICCS is an international sampling study with statistical uncertainty, and it describes a two-stage student selection procedure (schools, then classes), but it does not name any weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Therefore, weighting and replicate-weight usage cannot be confirmed from the provided text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report does not present any machine-learning model training/prediction on ICCS cognitive achievement outcomes, and it does not describe plausible-value (PV) generation/combining or missing-data imputation for PV-based achievement. Instead, it reports scale scores and percentages derived from ICCS instruments (knowledge test and questionnaire scales) using IEA/ICCS scaling procedures, without documenting PV handling or missing-data procedures in the provided excerpt. As a result, PV handling and missing-data handling are not reported in the text available here, representing a methodological transparency gap for PV/MV-specific processing.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Analytic sample corresponds to Swedish grade-8 students participating in ICCS 2016. The report states that 3,475 students from 155 schools participated with a 91% response rate, selected in two stages: first schools were sampled, then one class (teaching group) was sampled within each selected school. The report focuses on students’ responses to the knowledge test and questionnaires; no additional analytic exclusions (e.g., missing-item rules) are described in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This ICCS 2016 Swedish national report presents descriptive, scale-based results for grade-8 students (n=3,475) and compares Sweden to other participating countries and to ICCS 2009. It reports that Swedish students score very high on civic knowledge (mean 579; +62 vs international mean 517) and show a large improvement since 2009 (+42). For values and engagement, Sweden also shows strong support for equal opportunities (women/men mean 57; ethnic groups mean 57; immigrants mean 53) and increases over time in several engagement indicators, including discussion about politics/society outside school (+6.4) and civic self-efficacy (+2.6). The provided text does not include any machine-learning modeling, PV-combining strategy, or missing-data imputation procedure, so no ML performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/R²) are available and PV/MV handling cannot be verified from the excerpt.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction targets an official assessment framework, user guide, or technical manual without an empirical ML study. Sample sizes, ML algorithms, and predictive findings are intentionally null or empty per schema rules for non-empirical IEA/OECD documentation.
